subject: occupational-therapy
intro: Occupational therapy leads to the professions that rebuild everyday life — helping people regain the daily living skills, work roles and independence that illness, injury or disability interrupt.

roles.title: Occupational Therapists
roles.what: Assess, plan and organise rehabilitative programmes that build or restore vocational, homemaking and daily living skills — using therapeutic techniques, adapting environments, teaching skills and modifying the tasks that bar a person's independence.
roles.where: Units 1 and 2 — occupation-centred models and the OT process of evaluation, intervention and outcomes — are the working method; units 3 to 6 map the practice areas: paediatrics, physical rehabilitation, mental health and assistive technology.

roles.title: Occupational Therapy Assistants
roles.what: Assist occupational therapists in providing treatment — helping develop plans where state law allows, carrying out routine therapeutic functions, directing activity programmes and documenting the progress of treatments.
roles.where: Unit 2's intervention planning and unit 4's adaptive equipment and activity-based rehabilitation are what assistants deliver day to day; unit 3's school-based practice and unit 5's group work are common settings; unit 7's evidence strand guides documentation.

roles.title: Occupational Therapy Aides
roles.what: Under the close supervision of an occupational therapist or assistant, perform delegated, selected or routine tasks — preparing patients and treatment rooms, managing equipment and keeping therapy sessions running.
roles.where: Unit 4's adaptive equipment and splinting and unit 6's wheelchairs, seating and assistive technology explain the equipment aides prepare and maintain; unit 2's OT process shows how their support work fits each session.

roles.title: Recreational Therapists
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate medically approved recreation programmes in hospitals and nursing homes — sports, trips, dramatics, social activities and crafts — assessing each patient and recommending the activities that restore function.
roles.where: Unit 1's activity analysis and unit 2's goal setting are exactly the craft of turning leisure activity into therapy; unit 3's development and play grounds paediatric work; unit 5's group work and community mental health shape session design.
